seo.title: OTSO AI Hub case study · Codech
seo.description: How Codech built OTSO AI Hub: a private AI workspace for a regulated brokerage, with an AI document inventory and AI-powered team chat. Live in production in 37 days.
seo.og_title: OTSO AI Hub · a private AI workspace for files and team chat
seo.og_description: AI search, summaries and an assistant for every document, plus team chat where a shared file stays the governed original.

hero.headline: One private AI workspace for every file and every conversation
hero.sub: We designed and built OTSO AI Hub for a regulated brokerage. Staff store and share documents in one place, find them by meaning, get AI summaries and ask an assistant. Next, team chat keeps shared files inside the same rules.

stats: staff accounts, signed in with Microsoft

items.title: Scattered storage
items.body: KYC files, client agreements, trade records and policies lived in personal drives and email threads. Nobody had the full picture.

items.title: Search by filename only
items.body: Scanned PDFs and Chinese documents were effectively invisible. If you didn't know the file name, you didn't find the file.

items.title: Chat creates copies
items.body: A file sent in Teams is a detached copy: no classification, no version history, no access log, and no way to take it back.

decision.quote: A channel grants no document access. Ever.
paras: The shortcut was to reuse existing user groups as chat channels and get file sharing for free. We rejected it. Groups can be given whole drives, so adding someone to #deals would silently hand them every document ever posted there.

Instead, opening a file from chat runs the normal permission check against the document itself. Sharing stays the only way to grant access, so adding chat doesn't add a single new way for documents to leak.

notes: The workspace runs in the firm's own cloud (Tencent Cloud, Singapore). The assistant only ever sees documents the person asking is allowed to open.
128 staff were imported from the firm's Microsoft directory, with single sign-on and two-factor sign-in.

steps: Specs, then a clickable prototype of every screen that the client reviewed and approved.
Each production screen is screenshot-tested against the approved design. More than 0.1% drift fails the build.
Staging in week 4, production on day 37, and new modules like Team Chat added in slices.

cards: An assistant that can't be talked into a change
It can only propose actions; a person confirms each one. Sharing and downloading are outside what it can do at all, because document text is treated as untrusted input.
A 26 MB download took 14 attempts from Beijing. Resumable downloads fixed it, and an accelerated route measured 58% more throughput from China.
Every change writes an audit entry in the same database transaction, and the log is append-only at the database level, not just in code.
